This fire caused one firefighter death on 07/27/08.  He was doing reconnaissance work when a wind shift caused him to become entrapped.  The autopsy stated he died of burns and smoke inhalation.

On the evening of August 15, 2023, the Six Rivers National Forest experienced approximately 150 lightning strikes, which triggered the outbreak of wildfires. There were at least 27 confirmed fires as a result of the lightning strikes Out of 27 confirmed fires, 12 were located on the Gasquet Ranger District in Del Norte County, and they are included in the Smith River Complex. The wildfire was located 7 miles northeast of Gasquet, CA and spread into Oregon in far southeast Curry County and far southwest Josephine County, near the city of O'Brien. As of 0530 on 11/03/23, the total complex was 95,107 acres, 95 percent contained, had destroyed 12 structures, and cost $146 million dollars.  1,440 acres of the complex were in Josephine County, and an unknown amount in Curry County.

On the evening of August 15, 2023, lightning strikes triggered the outbreak of the Happy Camp Complex, with a total of 11 fires. They were located 21 miles west of Yreka, CA. It was burning in timber and heavy slash with several communities, and communications and energy infrastructure threatened. As of 0530 on 10/20, the complex was 21,725 acres, 100 percent contained, destroyed 9 structures, and cost 110.0 million dollars.

The Chilcoot Wildfire was started by lightning on August 24,2023 at 8:14 PM PST. The fire is located on the western edge of the Umpqua National Forest boundary. It is about 20 miles northeast of Glide, and 5 miles north of the Steamboat Creek junction at Highway 138. It is burning in steep terrain in the Chilcoot Ridge area and headwaters of Hipower Creek. As of 0530 on 10/20, it had burned 1,940 acres, was 100% contained, no structures had been lost, and it had cost 27.7 million dollars.

The Anvil Wildfire was discovered on August 25th at 1123 AM PST. The fire is located 7.5 miles east of Port Orford, on Anvil Mountain. The cause of the fire is undetermined. As of 530 AM PST on 10/20, it had burned 22,170 acres, was 100% contained, no structures had been destroyed, and it had cost 58.0 million dollars.

Low temperatures were generally in the upper 40s to mid 60s, and high temperatures in the mid 90s to 102 degrees. Strong high pressure brought excessive heat to the coastal/Coquille Valley portion of the south central Oregon coast from July 4th through July 9th. The excessive heat extended all the way to the coast during the peak of the heat wave from July 5th through July 6th. Low temperatures were in the lower 50s to lower 60s, and high temperatures mainly in the mid 80s to mid 90s, except 100 to 107 degrees in the Coquille Valley on July 5th and 6th. Record high temperatures were reached at the Southwest Oregon Regional Airport in North Bend of 84 degrees on July 5th and 86 degrees on July 6th. The Oregon State Medical Examiner's Office reported a potentially heat related death of a 33 year old male on July 7th.

The excessive heat extended all the way to the beaches at Brookings with a Chetco Effect of downslope northeast winds. Low temperatures were in the lower 50s to mid 70s, and high temperatures mainly in the lower 80s to mid 90s.

Report of 2 inch diameter tree branches breaking off, a large tree split in half at a Central Point city park and damaged picnic tables. Also, a home on willow springs road was destroyed when a Douglas Fir of approximately 2 feet in diameter landed on the roof.  This caused a bowing and break of the roof, and upheaval of the foundation.

Also, 7 roads were closed and power outages occurred that lasted 6 to 9 hours. Nearly two days of heavy rain, with amounts of around 1.50 to 2.50 inches, combined with snow melt caused the Pit River near Canby to rise to a peak above major flood stage. Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 06/21/08 ignited numerous fires across northern California. The Siskiyou Complex and the Blue 2 complex were still burning at the end of July...and have been combined as one entity. This fire caused one firefighter death on 07/27/08.

Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 06/21/08 ignited numerous fires across northern California. They started this day around 4:00 PM, but no resources were directed to this fire until July. It was still burning at the end of August, and consisted of the Bear Wallow and South Ukonom fires. In late August, this fire was transferred to NIMC and was considered to be low priority. However, information was available later on and as of 0630 PDT on 09/11/08, this fire was 47998 acres in size and 75% contained with an estimated containment date of 09/30/08. 13.8 million had been expended in fire fighting efforts.

Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 08/16/08 ignited a round of wildfires across southwest Oregon. The Lonesome Complex fires consisted of the Middle Fork, Lonesome, and Bessie Rock fires. As of 09/01/08, all but the Middle Fork fires were contained. The Middle Fork fire was still burning at the end of September. The size of the fire was 20687 acres and the was 45% contained. 17.7 million dollars had been spent on firefighting efforts.

Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 07/22/08 ignited another round of wildfires across northern California. The Panther Wildfire started this day around 3:00 AM. It was still burning at the end of September. As of 0800 PDT on 09/28/08, this fire was 52930 acres in size and 82% contained with an estimated containment date of 9/30/08. No update on expenditures was available, but 15.0 million had been expended in fire fighting efforts as of 08/31/08. This fire caused one firefighter death on 07/27/08.

Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 06/21/08 ignited numerous fires across northern California. They started this day around 4:00 PM, but no resources were directed to this fire until July. It was still burning at the end of September, and consisted of the Anthony Milne, Caribou and South Ukonom fires. As of 09/25/08, the fire was 50596 acres in size and was 86% contained with an estimated containment date of 09/30/08. Updated expenditures were not available, but as of 08/31/08, 13.8 million had been expended in fire fighting efforts.

Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 08/17/08 ignited another round of wildfires across southwest Oregon. The Rattle Fire was initially part of the North Fork Complex, but the other fires were suppressed. As of 09/30/08, the size of the fire was 18838 acres and was 65% contained. No updated expenditures was available, but as of 08/31/08, 1.9 million dollars had been spent on firefighting efforts.

A thunderstorm outbreak on 09/17/08 led to several wildfire starts across southern Oregon.  The Doubleday fire started at 17/1223 PDT and developed rapidly, threatening the community of Butte Falls.   It burned 1275 acres and  was contained at 21/1800 PDT.  No expenditure value was available for this fire.

Lightning from a thunderstorm event on 06/21/08 ignited numerous fires across northern California. The Siskiyou Complex and the Blue 2 complex were still burning at the end of September...and have been combined as one entity. As of 0800 PDT on 09/25/08, this fire was 87800 acres in size and 95% contained with an estimated containment date of 09/30/08. No update on expenditures was available, but as of 08/01/08, 62.5 million had been expended in fire fighting efforts.

A strong thunderstorm with frequent lightning caused structural damage...power outages...local urban flooding and one injury.  A McDonald's employee was injured when lightning struck the restaurant while he was unloading the dishwasher.  Full recovery was expected. A manufactured home was partially burned by a fire caused by a lightning strike.  Several intersections in Medford and Central Point were flooding by heavy rain.  More than 14,000 customers lost power at some point during the storm.  All but 891 of those customers had power restored within two hours.

This report came from www.avalanche.org. ||A party of 2 skiers was descending the west face of Garfield peak in Crater Lake National Park at 7800 ft.. The first skier was in the upper bowl when the slope avalanched with the crown 10-14 inches deep and approximately 900 ft. wide. He was carried down slope 400 vertical feet when he slammed into a stand of trees on the edge of the avalanche pathway above a small cliff. The snow continued down another 600 vertical feet to the road. He was partially buried and tangled on a tree. The other skier extricated him and assisted him to the road where he was then transported to the hospital. His main injury was a separated pelvis and was discharged 4 days later.

The first of a series of surges caused by the tsunami struck Port Orford at 07:11 PDT.  The maximum recorded amplitude was 2.02 meters which occurred around the seventh surge.  On the US West Coast, the only station that recorded a higher surge was Crescent City CA with a 2.47m amplitude. The surges gradually subsided during the next few days.  Major damage occurred at the Brookings Harbor, where 40% of the floating docks were destroyed and many boats were damaged or destroyed.  Docks, pilings, and channel buoys were also damaged at Gold Beach OR.  Four men were pulled into the ocean at Pistol River.  Two were rescued while the other two made it back to shore on their own.

A neighbor witnessed the tornado for about 1 minute. She heard a very loud noise and looked out the window where she saw ���a funnel cloud on the ground��� whipping around very fast and blowing apart a carport canopy sheltering a boat. The carport canopy was held down by four-gallon sized buckets filled with water. These buckets went flying into the boat and fence. The boat received a gash, and the metal pipe fence rail was broken. A satellite dish on the roof was also turned 90 degrees. The tornado then moved into an empty field and dissipated. There was no damage to the house, but the Christmas lights were pulled down.

An Ashland, Oregon man died while swimming in the Pacific Ocean at Whaleshead Beach State Park on Oregon's south coast Saturday, January 30th. Alexander Howell, 23, was swimming in the Pacific Ocean about 75 yards from shore with a friend, Alex Smith, age 22, from Medford, at about 2 p.m. when, according to witnesses, Howell indicated that he needed to go back to shore. Heavy surf and a strong rip current prevented the swimmers from making an easy return to shore, and the two got separated in the rough waters. Smith managed to get back to shore where two other friends were waiting but Howell was not able to get to shore and his friends were unable to initially find him. The group called 911 and searched the shoreline and found Howell unresponsive on the beach. The friends performed CPR until they were relieved by emergency responders. Howell was transported to Curry General Hospital in Gold Beach for advanced life support. He was declared deceased at the hospital.

The 42.3' steel-hulled crab fishing vessel Sarah Jo had a crew of 3. She was crossing the Coos bar around 4 pm local time, when the crankshaft broke, possibly as a result of rough conditions. After losing power, the boat then took a breaking wave on the bar, capsized, then sank. A USCG report shortly before the incident reported 10-12 foot steep breaking seas within the channel, and 8-10 foot steep seas just beyond the jetty. Conditions were worsening during rescue operations. Winds were south around 10 KT with 5 NM visibility. The bar was restricted to vessels below 40 feet. Note: The Sarah Jo was attempting to recover pots for the Eagle III, a crab fishing vessel that collided and broke up on the north jetty of Coos Bar on 01/19/2016, with the loss of 3 lives.||LOCATION: 43.355, -124.342: Within main channel of Coos Bar.||DEATHS: 1||MISSING PERSONS: 0||IMPACTS: All 3 crew were rescued from the water by the USCG and sent to the hospital. Raymundo Cardoso, 46, of Winchester Bay, later died from his injuries. Vessel sank in the channel and is most likely a complete loss. May also be a navigational obstruction.

events.event_narrative: At approximately 4:45 PM PDT on 10/26/18, a 14-foot aluminum boat lost power and drifted out into the Umpqua River Bar, where it capsized. Four people were on the |boat: a husband and wife, both 75, and their son and their son's friend, both in their 40s. The three men were subsequently found clinging to the boat and rescued by a 47-ft USCG motor life boat. Aside from being cold, all three were reported in good condition. The woman was found between the boat and the jetty, in an area with a high amount of debris. She was recovered by USCG helicopter and transported to a hospital, where she was pronounced deceased. As of 3:25 p.m., conditions at the Umpqua River Bar were reported as 6 to 8-foot swells, upwards of 14-foot breaking waves, light and variable winds, and a visibility of 3 miles. At 4:53 PM, Umpqua Offshore Buoy, 16 NM WNW of the Umpqua Bar, reported seas of 10.5 feet at 13 seconds, composed of 8.2 foot west swell at 13 seconds and a 5.9 foot wind wave (south).

It was discovered that a red 2020 Freightliner CMV operated by a 30-year-old male from Atwater California was traveling southbound and began to brake for vehicles slowing in front of him. Due to winter weather conditions, including icy roads, the semi tractor-trailer slid and crossed over into the oncoming lane and into a 2016 Mercedes SUV. The trailer portion of the semi collided with the Mercedes.  ODOT had been briefed over the weekend of possible icy roads due to melting snow and refreezing at night. No advisories were out at the time.

At around 9:10 AM PST on 12/12/20, a pickup truck on Highway 97 just north of the OR/CA border crossed the median and hit a southbound semi-truck. The driver of the pickup was killed, and his passenger and the semi-driver were seriously injured. As traffic backed up behind the scene, six more vehicles crashed and more than 10 left the roadway, including several semis. The highway was closed for more than four hours. Around the same time, Klamath Falls police were responding to another accident on Highway 97 just north of town, when another semi lost control and struck three police cars and a fire engine. The driver fled the scene and has not been apprehended as of the night of 12/12/20. Minutes after the first collision, another semi collided with the same fire truck, resulting in heavy damage. Oregon state police also reported numerous crashes on an icy Highway 39 near Merrill, OR (also just north of the CA/OR state line). Police reports stated nearly all involved were travelling too fast for icy road conditions. Road conditions at the time of the accident were reported to be icy due to overnight snow and ongoing freezing fog. The KLMT ASOS reported visibility of less than a quarter of a mile and freezing fog at the time of the accidents, with a temperature of 17 degrees. A cooperative observer at Keno, OR, around the same time as and near the scene of the fatal accident, reported 2.5 of snow in the previous 24 hours, with freezing fog and a temperature of 19 degrees at the time of observation.|Highway 97 was closed for over 4 hours. Three police cars and a fire truck, along with many civilian and commercial vehicles were heavily damaged. There were numerous injuries. A Freezing Fog Advisory issued for Klamath Falls and surrounding areas at 9:18 AM, effective until Noon PST.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM FLORENCE TO CAPE BLANCO OR OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Just before 9:30 AM PDT, the USCG received a report of a capsized vessel just outside of the Umpqua River Bar. The boat was a 22 ft pleasure craft with 5 people on board. Three made it to shore with assistance. A 5 year old girl and her grandmother were trapped in the cabin of the overturned vessel. They were recovered unresponsive by a USCG rescue swimmer, and were later pronounced deceased. Buoy 229, 15 nm west of the bar, reported 6' combined seas with a dominant period of 13 seconds around the time of the incident. North Bend (KOTH), 15 nm south of the incident, was reporting S-SSW winds of 8-13 kt with gusts up to 18 kt, with light rain, areas of fog, and low overcast. Water temperatures were roughly 55 degrees F.

A mudslide coming down Whitney Creek on the northwest slope of Mount Shasta impacted Highway 97. This occurred at 0507 PDT on 09/10/21.  0.4 to 0.7 inches of rain fell in the area over four hours. This slide was likely due to the rainfall, combined with glacial melt from the Whitney Glacier.  The slide closed Highway 97 for a short time, and one semitrailer truck was stuck in the mud.  No injuries or fatalities occurred.
